nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$ and all divisors $D_1, D_2$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the evaluation of a divisor $D$ against $f$, we have $f(D_1 + D_2) = f(D_1) \, f(D_2)$.
nodes.title: Evaluation is multiplicative

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ equals $\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$, the product over the points in the support of $D$.
nodes.title: Evaluation is a product over the support

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$ and a function $f : C \to G$, this is the monoid homomorphism from the group of divisors on $C$, written multiplicatively, to $G$ that sends a divisor $D$ to the finite product $\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of divisors as a group homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$, every point $P \in C$ and every integer $n$, the divisor $n \cdot P$, with coefficient $n$ at $P$ and $0$ elsewhere, evaluates against $f$ to $f(P)^n$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a one-point divisor

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$ and every function $f : C \to G$, the evaluation of the zero divisor on $C$ against $f$ is the identity element $1$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The zero divisor evaluates to one

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$, every integer $n$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the evaluation of $D$ against $f$, we have $f(nD) = f(D)^n$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of an integer multiple

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, a function $f : C \to G$ and a divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ is the element $f(D) = \prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a divisor against a function

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
